mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes R 280 CDI or 320 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM642 engine for the R 280 CDI or R 320 CDI costs £2,800-£4,600 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - the OM642 V6 requires specialist knowledge for proper installation.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes R 320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start between 900-1,200rpm is the classic warning sign on the OM642 engine. If ignored, it can lead to engine seizure and catastrophic failure.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes R 280 CDI or 320 CDI engine (OM642) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 is fundamentally robust, but R Class owners should be aware of timing chain stretch between 80,000-120,000 miles, oil cooler seal degradation, and swirl flap failure. With these addressed, the engine is capable of 150,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes R 280 CDI and 320 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM642 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work is needed. One owner reported 200,000 km (124,000 miles) with the engine still running.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes R 280 CDI or 320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the R Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM642 costs £2,800-£4,600 - comparable to the value of a £3,000-£8,000 vehicle, making it a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes R 280 CDI or 320 CDI need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 - typically 5W-30. The OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5 litres with filter.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz R Class 280 CDI/320 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The R 320 CDI launched with the W251 generation in 2006 as the core diesel variant, powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel producing 224hp. The R 280 CDI joined the range as the entry-level diesel in September 2006, using the same 3.0-litre V6 turbodiesel engine but electronically restricted to 188bhp. Both variants shared the same 7-speed automatic transmission and permanent 4MATIC all-wheel drive system, with the R 280 available in short-wheelbase form to keep it below the £40,000 mark. Production continued until 2012 for UK models.

milestones.description: OM642.950, 3.0L V6 diesel, 224hp @ 3,800rpm (R 320 CDI, W251 launch)
September 2006 - OM642.950, 3.0L V6 diesel, 188hp @ 4,000rpm (R 280 CDI, entry-level, electronically restricted)
2009 - R 280 CDI and R 320 CDI available in standard and 4MATIC variants
R 280 CDI replaced by R 300 CDI in facelift range
2012 - R 320 CDI continues as core diesel variant through to end of UK production

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz R Class 280 CDI/320 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The R 280 CDI and R 320 CDI's OM642 V6 diesel is a fundamentally robust engine, but it has well-documented weaknesses that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The most critical issue is timing chain stretch and guide wear, followed by oil cooler seal degradation and swirl flap failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM642 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Failure
problems.h4: OM642 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Failure - The R 280/320 CDI's Most Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: The rear-mounted timing chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure over time, allowing the chain to stretch and plastic guides to wear. Cold-start rattling between 900-1,200rpm is the classic warning sign. If ignored, guide fragments can enter the oil sump, causing catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain tension, guide swap, and updated tensioner fit without engine removal
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles if caught before rattling escalates

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine removal, bench rebuild with upgraded timing assembly, new seals, supply & fit installation

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2006-2012 R 280 CDI or R 320 CDI is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000 depending on mileage and condition. These large luxury MPVs have suffered significant depreciation, meaning replacement costs can approach or exceed vehicle value. For well-maintained examples with good bodywork and transmission health, replacement remains justifiable.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a metallic rattle on cold start between 900-1,200rpm, act immediately. A preventative chain and guide replacement is cost-effective on low-mileage examples. Once plastic guide fragments enter the oil sump or the tensioner fully collapses, a complete OM642 rebuilt engine is the safer, more economical route.

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Degradation - Coolant Contamination Risk
problems.rootCause: Factory rubber sealing rings degrade under repeated thermal cycles, allowing pressurised engine oil to leak directly into the coolant matrix. This is a labour-intensive repair due to the oil cooler's location in the V of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine disassembly to cooler housing, new gasket fit, coolant flush, pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-60k miles; viable only if coolant is clean

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete unit swap with factory-upgraded seal materials, new oil cooler pre-fitted, supply & fit
repairOptions.longevity: Lifetime of vehicle when combined with regular servicing

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical R 280/320 CDI is worth £3,000-£8,000.
problems.recommendation: Accessing the oil cooler on the R Class requires significant component removal. If the coolant shows milky contamination or the engine has run hot, a patch repair is a false economy. A rebuilt OM642 engine arrives with upgraded cooler seals already fitted, eliminating the most labour-intensive step.

problems.group: OM642 Swirl Flap & EGR Cooler Failure
problems.h4: OM642 Swirl Flap & EGR Cooler Failure - Power Loss and Emissions Issues
problems.rootCause: Heavy carbon deposits cause swirl flap shafts to seize or snap, while the EGR cooler housing cracks under thermal stress, mixing exhaust gases into the cooling system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake manifold removal, carbon decarbonisation, swirl flap replacement, new EGR cooler fit
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-50k miles; temporary fix on high-soot engines

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine exchange with revised intake routing, upgraded cooler, new injectors, supply & fit
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles with resolved emissions & boost delivery

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical R 280/320 CDI is worth £3,000-£8,000.
problems.recommendation: Component replacement works if caught early and driving patterns include regular motorway use. However, if broken flap fragments enter cylinders or the EGR cooler has contaminated the coolant circuit, a full rebuilt OM642 engine is the only reliable long-term solution.
